provenance: Telephone call, 2026-09-03, Larry's son asking the tier-1 questions from the interview guide and typing Larry's answers as he spoke them. The Camp Zama date question had been promoted to the head of the guide that morning. Raw capture: research/interviews/breakfast-questions.md, annotated in place under each question.
text: They were a free news paper, like 6 pages. I think the first page on the right side was 40 guys killed.
researchNotes: RECORDED AS REOPENING THE EDITION QUESTION, AND THAT READING IS RETRACTED THE SAME DAY. The reasoning was: a six-page free paper with casualties on page one does not fit the Five-Star Edition, which runs 24-37 pages with lists on inside pages, so perhaps he read something else. That inverted the weight of his own words. HE HEDGED THE PAGE DETAIL AND NOT THE TITLE - "I think the first page on the right side" - and the title is the part he has given firm and repeatedly: volunteered in the original project brief (2026-brief-kia-report.json), confirmed in the ward question of 2026-08-23 (giscus-stories-c18118868.json), and validated with him directly by his son more than once. Weighting a hedged detail against an unhedged, repeatedly confirmed one is the exact failure this archive had already written down twice on 2026-09-03: check his account against the best source before discounting it. WHAT STANDS: it was Stars and Stripes. WHAT REMAINS GENUINELY OPEN, as an oddity in his account rather than evidence against the title: why six pages. Plausible readings, none to be put to him - he was handed or found a SECTION rather than a whole paper, which is ordinary in a hospital ward where papers are pulled apart; or "the first page on the right side" means the right-hand COLUMN of the front page he was holding, since casualty matter ran in columns; or a page count at sixty-one years is simply soft, which is why he hedged it. AND THE DETAIL EARNS ITS KEEP IF READ AS A POINTER RATHER THAN A CONTRADICTION: the sweeps so far have targeted the dense inside casualty lists, found at pp.32, 19, 13 and 4. His memory describes something on a FRONT page with a number attached - about forty dead. That is a different kind of item from the inside list, and the front pages of the 3-7 September 1965 issues should be read as well as the list pages.
